h: Big Names, a Welsh Dinosaur and a Giant Turtle
p: Art lovers, keep an eye out for Renoir's La Parisienne, often nicknamed the Blue Lady, which is one of the best-loved paintings in the collection, along with Monet's water lilies and works by Van Gogh and Cézanne. Seeing big names like that for free in the middle of Cardiff is a proper treat.

Down in natural history, the stars include the enormous leatherback turtle that was found washed up on the Welsh coast near Harlech, and Dracoraptor, a small meat-eating dinosaur discovered on the beach near Penarth, just down the road. Kids get a buzz knowing the dinosaur came from practically on their doorstep. The Clore Discovery Centre has given families a hands-on space to handle real specimens, so ask staff what's running during your visit.

Give yourselves two to three hours to dip into both art and science without everyone flagging. Just outside, Alexandra Gardens holds the Welsh National War Memorial, and the grand civic buildings of Cathays Park make for a handsome stroll. If the museum leaves you wanting more, its sister site St Fagans National Museum of History, on the edge of Cardiff, is also free and brings Welsh life through the ages to life with rebuilt houses, shops and workshops.
